propositions.text: Whether the Federal Court can order an interim stay on its own motion on a Charter issue unrelated to immigration.
propositions.quote: More specifically, the issue to be decided is whether the Motion Judge could, on his own motion, raise at the hearing an issue pursuant to the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms... and order an interim stay of the respondent’s removal

paragraphs.summary: The court states the issue is whether the Federal Court could on its own raise a Charter issue unrelated to immigration and order an interim stay of removal.

propositions.text: The Federal Court's action was inappropriate, unwarranted, and beyond its jurisdiction; appeal will be granted and order quashed.
propositions.quote: this course of action was not only inappropriate and unwarranted, but more importantly, in excess of the Federal Court’s jurisdiction

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the Federal Court exceeded its jurisdiction and will grant the appeal and quash the interlocutory order.

propositions.text: Respondent is a UK citizen subject to a removal order for serious criminality based on UK convictions.
propositions.quote: The respondent... is the subject of a removal order because he was declared inadmissible... on grounds of serious criminality

propositions.text: IRB issued a deportation order based on offences including one punishable by at least ten years imprisonment under IRPA.
propositions.quote: one of which... would constitute an offence punishable by a maximum term of imprisonment of at least ten years pursuant to paragraph 36(1)(b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act

propositions.text: Respondent also charged with offences in Canada from 2013 to 2019, not part of IRB's inadmissibility assessment.
propositions.quote: The respondent was also charged with offences in Canada from 2013 to 2019, which did not form part of the IRB’s inadmissibility assessment

paragraphs.summary: The court states the respondent is a UK citizen subject to a removal order for serious criminality based on UK convictions and Canadian charges not considered by IRB.

propositions.text: Respondent filed applications for leave and judicial review of the 2019 inadmissibility decision and removal order; one is pending, one dismissed.
propositions.quote: The respondent filed an application for leave and judicial review of the 2019 inadmissibility decision... decision on leave is still pending... judicial review of the IRB’s 2019 removal order... dismissed

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the respondent filed judicial review applications of inadmissibility and removal decisions, with one pending and one dismissed.

propositions.text: Respondent's removal scheduled for March 6, 2023, deferred and rescheduled multiple times due to refusals and medical issues.
propositions.quote: The respondent was first scheduled for removal on March 6, 2023, but the removal was deferred and rescheduled... removal was again postponed due to a medical issue

propositions.text: CBSA refused deferral request on March 30, 2023; judicial review of refusal dismissed April 12, 2023.
propositions.quote: request for deferral, which was refused by the Canada Border Services Agency... application for judicial review... dismissed

paragraphs.summary: The court describes the respondent's removal was deferred multiple times, with deferral requests refused and judicial review dismissed.

propositions.text: Respondent requested deferral again based on prior rejected arguments and pending medical diagnosis and applications; CBSA refused on May 31, 2023.
propositions.quote: The respondent again requested a deferral... arguments previously rejected... CBSA refused on May 31, 2023

paragraphs.summary: The court states the respondent requested another deferral based on prior rejected arguments and pending matters, which CBSA refused.

propositions.text: On June 1, 2023, respondent filed judicial review application of CBSA refusal and motion to stay removal; hearing on June 6, 2023.
propositions.quote: On June 1, 2023, Mr. Ewen then filed... application for leave and judicial review... as well as a motion to stay the removal

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the respondent filed judicial review and stay motion on June 1, 2023, with hearing on June 6, 2023.

propositions.text: At hearing start, parties had no preliminary matters; Motion Judge raised a new issue on his own initiative.
propositions.quote: At the start of the hearing, the parties were asked if they had any preliminary matters... The Motion Judge then raised on his own initiative a new issue

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Motion Judge raised a new issue on his own initiative at the hearing start, surprising the parties.

propositions.text: Motion Judge questioned use of pronouns in submissions, asked if use of 'they/their' violated respondent's Charter right to gender identity.
propositions.quote: The Motion Judge proceeded to highlight the use of “he” and “him”... asked the appellant’s counsel whether the use of “they/their” pronouns allegedly violated the respondent’s Charter right to his gender identity

propositions.text: Respondent identifies as 'he' and finds use of 'they/their' confusing and affecting his dignity.
propositions.quote: COLIN JAMES EWEN: I identify as a he... It is pretty confusing as well... It’s not very direct... It does affect my dignity

paragraphs.summary: The court describes the Motion Judge's inquiry into pronoun use and the respondent's identification as 'he' and dignity concerns.

propositions.text: Motion Judge directed parties to file written submissions on whether gender identification is a protected Charter right and if violated, and appropriate remedy.
propositions.quote: The Motion Judge then directed the parties to file written submissions on three questions on the issue of gender identification and the Charter

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Motion Judge ordered written submissions on gender identification as a Charter right and possible violation and remedy.

propositions.text: Court granted an interim stay of removal to receive submissions, without final determination of stay motion.
propositions.quote: The Court made no final determination of the stay motion, but instead granted an interim stay of the removal

paragraphs.summary: The court notes an interim stay was granted to receive submissions, without deciding the stay motion finally.

propositions.text: Removal cancelled due to interim stay; future removal would allow new deferral requests and judicial review.
propositions.quote: In light of the Order granting an interim stay, the removal was cancelled... Mr. Ewen will have the opportunity to make another request for deferral

paragraphs.summary: The court explains removal was cancelled due to interim stay; future removal would allow new deferral and judicial review requests.

propositions.text: Appellant filed notice of appeal and motion for stay of Order; this Court granted stay pending appeal and expedited appeal.
propositions.quote: the appellant filed a notice of appeal and brought a motion for a stay of the Order pending this appeal... This Court exceptionally granted a stay

propositions.text: Appellant requested expedited appeal and consented to respondent not being removed pending final judgment.
propositions.quote: The appellant also consented to an order that, pending final judgment in this appeal, the respondent shall not be removed from Canada

paragraphs.summary: The court states the appellant appealed and sought a stay, which this Court granted and expedited, with consent to no removal pending judgment.

propositions.text: Three issues: jurisdiction to hear appeal; Federal Court's error or excess of jurisdiction; whether to refer stay motion back.
propositions.quote: This appeal raises three issues: Does this Court have jurisdiction... Did the Federal Court err... should this Court refer the stay motion back

paragraphs.summary: The court identifies three issues: jurisdiction to hear appeal, Federal Court's error or excess, and whether to refer stay motion back.

propositions.text: Interlocutory decisions in immigration matters are generally not appealable under IRPA paragraph 72(2)(e).
propositions.quote: interlocutory decisions in immigration matters are not ordinarily subject to appeals pursuant to the preclusive clause contained in paragraph 72(2)(e) of IRPA

propositions.text: Appeal from final judgment requires certification of a serious question of general importance under IRPA paragraph 74(d).
propositions.quote: an appeal from a final judgment is only available when the judge rendering it certifies a serious question of general importance (see paragraph 74(d) of IRPA)

paragraphs.summary: The court explains IRPA generally bars appeals from interlocutory decisions and requires certification for appeals from final judgments.

propositions.text: Federal Courts Act paragraph 27(1)(c) authorizes appeal from interlocutory Federal Court judgments.
propositions.quote: paragraph 27(1)(c) of the Federal Courts Act... authorizes an appeal from an interlocutory judgment of the Federal Court

propositions.text: Jurisprudence allows exceptional appeals of interlocutory decisions despite IRPA bars.
propositions.quote: a body of jurisprudence has developed, empowering this Court in exceptional circumstances to entertain an appeal of an interlocutory decision... despite the statutory bars found in the IRPA

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Federal Courts Act allows interlocutory appeals and jurisprudence permits exceptional appeals despite IRPA bars.

propositions.text: Appellate review may be available for fundamental or exceptional matters striking at rule of law (Subhaschandran, Mahjoub).
propositions.quote: appellate review may be available when a case raises “very fundamental matters” or “truly exceptional matters” that “strike right at the rule of law”

propositions.text: Exception to no appeal rule for separate, divisible judicial acts involving powers outside IRPA (Harkat, Tobiass).
propositions.quote: Where the alleged error has been made in the context of a “separate, divisible judicial act”, and involves the exercise of a power that is not found in the IRPA, appellate review is not governed by that Act

paragraphs.summary: The court cites precedent allowing appeals for fundamental matters or separate judicial acts outside IRPA's scope.

propositions.text: This case exemplifies exception: Motion Judge's interim stay on Charter pronoun issue has no basis in IRPA.
propositions.quote: The Motion Judge’s decision to order an interim stay to inquire into... has no basis in the IRPA’s provisions

propositions.text: IRPA preclusive clauses do not apply in these exceptional circumstances.
propositions.quote: The preclusive clauses found in paragraphs 72(2)(e) and 74(d) of IRPA therefore cannot find application in the very particular and exceptional circumstances of this case

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the Motion Judge's interim stay on a Charter pronoun issue is outside IRPA and preclusive clauses do not apply here.

propositions.text: Federal Court exceeded jurisdiction by raising a new Charter issue unrelated to parties' framed issues or stay motion.
propositions.quote: The Federal Court exceeded its jurisdiction by unilaterally raising a new Charter issue that did not stem from the issues as framed by the parties

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Federal Court exceeded jurisdiction by raising a new unrelated Charter issue unilaterally.

propositions.text: Motion Judge admitted raising a surprise issue of personal interest before parties addressed stay motion merits.
propositions.quote: the Motion Judge put an issue to the parties that was of particular interest to him, and that he knew such issue would come as a surprise to the parties

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the Motion Judge raised a surprise issue of personal interest before addressing the stay motion merits.

propositions.text: Motion Judge reviewed parties' records on pronoun usage and noted inconsistency in appellant's submissions
propositions.quote: The Motion Judge then proceeded to take the appellant’s counsel through both parties’ records, highlighting the usage of “he” and “him” in reference to the respondent, and contrasted that usage with the inconsistent use of “he/him” and “they/their” pronouns in the appellant’s written submissions.

propositions.text: Motion Judge was not satisfied by appellant's counsel's oral explanation of gender-neutral pronouns
propositions.quote: Not being satisfied by the appellant’s counsel’s oral response at the hearing that attempted to clarify its usage of “they/their” pronouns as gender-neutral terminology, and counsel’s apology for any confusion caused

propositions.text: Motion Judge adjourned hearing and ordered interim stay until Charter issue could be argued and decided
propositions.quote: the Motion Judge adjourned the hearing and ordered an interim stay until the Charter issue, that he had himself identified, could be argued in a separate hearing and be ultimately decided.

paragraphs.summary: The Motion Judge reviewed pronoun usage, was unsatisfied with appellant's explanation, and ordered an interim stay for a Charter issue hearing.

propositions.text: Supreme Court in R. v. Mian guides appellate courts to raise new issues sparingly and only in rare circumstances
propositions.quote: In R. v. Mian, 2014 SCC 54 [Mian], the Supreme Court provided some guidance as to when and how appellate courts should exercise their discretion to raise new issues... it should be used sparingly and “only in rare circumstances”

propositions.text: New issues should be raised only if failing to do so risks injustice, sufficient record exists, and no procedural prejudice results
propositions.quote: a new issue should only be raised “when failing to do so would risk an injustice”, “whether there is a sufficient record on which to raise the issue”, and where it would not result in “procedural prejudice to any party”

propositions.text: These principles apply by analogy to reviewing courts in summary procedures
propositions.quote: these guiding principles... apply by analogy with equal force to a reviewing court, especially in a summary procedure

propositions.text: Motion Judge failed to properly exercise discretion in raising a new issue
propositions.quote: In the case at bar, I find that the Motion Judge failed to properly exercise his discretion in raising a new issue.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Motion Judge erred by raising a new issue without proper discretion, guided by Supreme Court principles from R. v. Mian.

propositions.text: Failure to raise section 15 Charter issue did not cause injustice to respondent once confusion was clarified
propositions.quote: I fail to see how the failure to raise the section 15 Charter issue would have worked an injustice to the respondent, especially once the confusion was clarified at the hearing.

propositions.text: Respondent, though self-represented, did not convincingly claim dignity affected by pronoun use
propositions.quote: His tentative answer at the hearing when prompted by the Court is far from convincing in this respect.

propositions.text: Appellant's counsel was prejudiced by Motion Judge's unexpected reasoning and interim stay order
propositions.quote: it is clear that counsel for the appellant was prejudiced by the Motion Judge’s unexpected line of reasoning to order an interim stay.

propositions.text: Appellant was later allowed to address concerns in writing but at cost of enforcement and timely decision
propositions.quote: Of course, the appellant was given the opportunity to address the Motion Judge’s concerns in writing at a later date, but that was done at the expense of being able to enforce a removal order and to have a timely decision of the Court on the motion for a stay of the Direction to report.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no injustice to respondent from not raising Charter issue, notes appellant's prejudice from interim stay, and respondent's weak claim.

propositions.text: No sufficient record existed to raise the Charter issue, especially important for Charter claims
propositions.quote: there was no sufficient record on which to raise the Charter issue. This consideration is particularly important when a new issue raised relates to the Charter.

propositions.text: Raising Charter claim without sufficient evidence exceeded Motion Judge's jurisdiction and impartial role
propositions.quote: By raising a claim of Charter infringement absent a sufficient evidentiary record, the Motion Judge exceeded his jurisdiction and overstepped his role as an independent and impartial judicial decision-maker.

propositions.text: Supreme Court warns courts should not seek out wrongs to right (Mian at para. 42)
propositions.quote: he could be seen as going “in search of a wrong to right” (Mian at para. 42).

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Motion Judge exceeded jurisdiction by raising a Charter claim without sufficient record, citing Supreme Court caution.

propositions.text: Courts and tribunals should not raise new section 15 Charter issues on their own initiative
propositions.quote: this Court and the Supreme Court have cautioned that an administrative tribunal should not raise a new section 15 Charter issue on its own initiative

propositions.text: Weatherley v. Canada and Kahkewistahaw First Nation v. Taypotat prohibit raising section 15 Charter issues without factual record
propositions.quote: see, for example, Weatherley v. Canada (Attorney General), 2021 FCA 158 at para. 20... Kahkewistahaw First Nation v. Taypotat, 2015 SCC 30... error for court of appeal to decide appeal on section 15 violation absent factual record

paragraphs.summary: The court cites precedent forbidding courts or tribunals from raising new section 15 Charter issues without factual record.

propositions.text: Requisite elements to determine Charter issue were absent: no claim, no evidence, no issue raised, no remedy sought, no evidence or cross-examination
propositions.quote: There was no statement of claim or notice of application alleging a Charter breach... no evidence before the Federal Court... respondent did not raise the issue... no opportunity to file evidence or to cross-examine.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no procedural or evidentiary foundation existed to determine the Charter issue in this case.

propositions.text: Supreme Court requires courts not to resolve Charter issues in factual vacuum
propositions.quote: From the very early cases dealing with Charter issues, the Supreme Court has made it crystal clear that courts must not resolve them in a factual vacuum.

propositions.text: Mackay v. Manitoba and other cases emphasize need for evidence linking government action to section 15 infringement
propositions.quote: As the Court stated in Mackay v. Manitoba... It is for a claimant to demonstrate, through evidence, that there is a nexus between government action and an alleged section 15 infringement.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Supreme Court authority requiring evidence to support Charter claims and forbidding decisions in factual vacuum.

propositions.text: Urgent stay motions are inappropriate to assess new Charter claims not raised in underlying judicial review
propositions.quote: An urgent motion for a stay is obviously not the appropriate procedure to assess a new Charter claim, especially when the issue has not been raised by the parties in the underlying application for judicial review.

propositions.text: Stay motions are summary, expedited, with limited record and procedural rights lacking for Charter issues
propositions.quote: These motions, by their very nature, are dealt with expeditiously and on the basis of a stripped-down record, and many of the procedural rights required for a Charter issue to be properly litigated and adjudicated are lacking.

propositions.text: Further submissions ordered by Motion Judge do not cure procedural shortcomings for Charter issues
propositions.quote: Further submissions, as ordered by the Motion Judge, will not cure these shortcomings.

propositions.text: Federal Court Charter decisions may be immune from appellate review due to IRPA section 72 and certified question requirement
propositions.quote: a decision of the Federal Court on the Charter issue could be immune from appellate review as a result of section 72 of IRPA and the requirement of there being a certified question.

propositions.text: Federal Courts Act subsection 18.2 does not authorize interim declarations in interim stay context because declarations are final
propositions.quote: subsection 18.2 of the Federal Courts Act does not authorize the granting of interim declarations in the context of an interim stay for relief, because declarations are final

paragraphs.summary: The court finds stay motions unsuitable for new Charter claims, procedural rights lacking, and interim declarations unauthorized in this context.

propositions.text: The Order is fundamentally flawed and should be quashed
propositions.quote: I am of the view that the Order is fundamentally flawed and should be quashed.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the Order is flawed and must be quashed.

propositions.text: Respondent argues Federal Court properly exercised jurisdiction to ensure fair and equal treatment
propositions.quote: the respondent argued that the Federal Court properly exercised its jurisdiction in issuing the Order and the interim stay because... it was managing its proceedings to ensure that he was treated fairly and equally.

propositions.text: Respondent correctly notes judges must ensure equality and fairness to self-represented litigants
propositions.quote: The respondent is correct to point out that judges are advised to ensure equality in its proceedings, as well as to ensure that self-represented litigants are treated fairly

paragraphs.summary: The respondent argues the Federal Court acted properly to ensure fairness; the court agrees judges must ensure equality and fairness to self-represented litigants.

propositions.text: Procedural fairness principles do not authorize judges to exceed Federal Courts Act scope or advocate for parties
propositions.quote: these principles are not a licence to circumvent the scope of the Federal Courts Act... not meant to authorize the judge to stray from their role as a neutral arbiter... or to advocate on behalf of a party

propositions.text: There is a line between procedural fairness and raising new substantive questions absent from parties' submissions
propositions.quote: There is a line to be drawn between ensuring a procedurally fair process... and raising a new substantive question... absent from the parties’ submissions

paragraphs.summary: The court finds procedural fairness does not permit judges to raise new substantive issues beyond parties' submissions or act as advocates.

propositions.text: Normal course is to refer matter back to Federal Court to adjudicate underlying stay motion
propositions.quote: the normal course of action would be to refer the matter back to the Federal Court so as to adjudicate the underlying motion for a stay.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the usual remedy is to refer the stay motion back to the Federal Court for adjudication.

propositions.text: Appellant claims stay motion became moot after removal cancellation and no live controversy remains
propositions.quote: the appellant claims that when the respondent’s removal was cancelled, the stay motion became moot because there was no longer a live controversy between the parties

propositions.text: Appellant argues this Court should not decide moot matters and relies on Borowski
propositions.quote: He argues that this is not a case in which this Court should exercise its discretion to decide a moot matter: Borowski

propositions.text: Appellant relies on principle that courts should avoid deciding questions with no practical effect or useful purpose
propositions.quote: He also relies on the principle that courts should refrain from deciding questions where there is no obvious, useful purpose to be served by granting the relief sought or where a proceeding would have no practical effect.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the stay motion is moot and this Court should avoid deciding moot or impractical questions.

propositions.text: It is unnecessary to decide mootness; underlying stay motion cannot proceed given circumstances
propositions.quote: It is not necessary for the resolution of this matter to decide whether or not the stay motion is moot... the underlying motion for a stay can no longer proceed and should not proceed given the following circumstances.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds mootness need not be decided as the stay motion cannot proceed under current circumstances.

propositions.text: Respondent is no longer subject to imminent enforced removal; removal was cancelled by CBSA
propositions.quote: The respondent is no longer subject to an imminent enforced removal... removal... was cancelled by the CBSA.

propositions.text: Future enforcement steps include new interview, removal date, direction to report, deferral request, judicial review, and stay motion
propositions.quote: any future enforcement of the removal order will involve the following steps: A new pre-removal interview; A new removal date; A new direction to report; The opportunity for the respondent to submit a request for deferral of removal; and A further opportunity... to submit an application for leave and judicial review, as well as a new motion for a stay of removal.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the respondent's removal was cancelled and future enforcement would require new procedural steps.

propositions.text: Respondent would have opportunity to request deferral, apply for judicial review, and seek stay on fresh record if enforcement resumed
propositions.quote: If the appellant were to choose to take these steps, the respondent would have an opportunity to make a request for deferral of removal... and could once again seek an urgent stay of removal on the basis of a fresh evidentiary record and of an updated set of circumstances.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds respondent could seek deferral, judicial review, and stay on a fresh record if removal enforcement resumed.

propositions.text: Returning stay motion to Federal Court would not promote judicial economy or serve useful purpose
propositions.quote: Returning the stay motion to the Federal Court would not promote judicial economy and would serve no useful purpose.

propositions.text: Stay motions are summary, urgent, with bare record and limited time for consideration
propositions.quote: Stay motions are meant to be summary proceedings to deal with an urgent situation, with a bare bone record and very little time for the Court to ponder the issues raised by the parties.

propositions.text: Referring stay motion back would mean decision on stale record and outdated circumstances, limiting relevance
propositions.quote: Were this Court to refer the stay motion back to the Federal Court, it would be argued based on a stale record and on a set of circumstances over five months out of date, making any decision on the motion of limited relevance and usefulness.

propositions.text: Preferable to leave issues for Federal Court's consideration in underlying judicial review or new stay motion with current record
propositions.quote: Now that Mr. Ewen is no longer subject to an imminent enforced removal... it is preferable to leave the issues... for the consideration of the Federal Court in the context of the underlying judicial review application or a contemporaneous record should a new motion for stay of removal be made.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds returning the stay motion would be futile due to stale record and prefers issues be considered in underlying or new motions.

propositions.text: Appeal granted and Federal Court’s interlocutory Order of June 6, 2023 set aside
propositions.quote: I would grant the appeal and set aside the Federal Court’s interlocutory Order of June 6, 2023.

propositions.text: Stay motion not referred back to Federal Court as it would serve no useful purpose
propositions.quote: I would not refer the underlying stay motion back to the Federal Court, as this would serve no useful purpose.

propositions.text: Interim stay ordered by this Court on June 29, 2023 lifted with respect to application for leave and judicial review
propositions.quote: The interim stay ordered by this Court on June 29, 2023 of all proceedings in file IMM-6831-23 should be lifted with respect to the application for leave and judicial review.

propositions.text: No costs awarded in this appeal
propositions.quote: There shall be no costs in this appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The court grants the appeal, sets aside the order, lifts the interim stay, refuses to refer back, and orders no costs.
